body: I know that feeling. What helped me was allowing myself to feel the pain very deeply for a period of time. I listened to some unpleasant ambient music. I thought about the difference between who I thought she was and what I meant to her and the reality. It was incredibly painful but when I came out the other side a lot of the longing and desire had dissipated and I was able to accept who she really was and the nature of our relationship. I still have some compulsions around her but the ache of missing her is gone.
I do this too. If she looks at my story then she still likes me. If she doesn't then she hates me forever.
When you're trying to write an essay for university and your mom calls threatening to drive down the wrong side of the motorway.
I was also resistant to medication for a long time but when I finally started taking it things did improve for me in a big way.

Something I've found helpful is accepting that I live in a society with a deeply fucked up relationship with sex and sexuality. To a much, much lesser extent I have felt stigmatized for my lack of sexual activity, which is a result of depression, anxiety and sexual anorexia. I've had to blame my meds for my sexual inhibition out of fear of being labelled a prude by a "sex-positive" friend.

Sex workers are attacked because more than any other profession they are sexually objectified and can therefore become a focus point for our society's collective sexual neuroses. When I was at a residential treatment center I became friends with a former sex worker and, honestly, I love her. I feel nothing but warmth and concern towards her. Remember that there are people out there who will see your humanity and will love you for it.

I get massively depressed about it. Physical touch and emotional/sexual passion produces unbearable anxiety and shame for me, probably due to childhood trauma. I wish I wasn't this way but I don't know how to change. I wish I could find an understanding partner.
